title: Price sensitivity & operational stress lattice - Jun 15 2026
summary: Workbook for mapping joint price & demand shocks into headcount and cash outcomes using a probability lattice. Focused on operational triggers (hiring freeze, slab re-pricing, burst-capacity sell-down) and short-term mitigations to preserve runway while protecting SLAs.
objective: Produce a compact decision grid that ties observed price pressure and demand variance to concrete HC and pricing actions, with estimated month-by-month P&L impact and recommended thresholds for Q3–Q4 2026.
assumptions: Base token revenue growth: +18% QoQ for active cohorts in hosted API unless explicitly compressed
Unit price elasticity: -0.6 (i.e., 10% price drop -> +6% demand) as a central estimate; high-variance cohort elasticity +/-0.4
Average token cost (inference) per 1k tokens: $0.018 baseline; quantization & batching improvements can reduce to $0.013 with 8–12 weeks ramp
Hiring lead time: 8 weeks for senior infra/ops, 4–6 weeks for associate roles; contractor conversion cost multiplier = 1.6
Dedicated capacity bookings are ~15% of forecasted demand and have contractual minimums that limit short-term capacity reductions
Runway buffer target (finance policy): 16 months at current burn without backstop measures
scenarios: Scenario A - Benign: price stable, demand follows base growth; no immediate HC action
Scenario B - Price Compression: realized average per-token price drops 12% across mass-market customers; demand increases 4%; margin contraction triggers review
Scenario C - Demand Collapse: enterprise churn +30% in 60 days due to competitor SLAs; tokens decline 22% with moderate price pressure
Scenario D - Surge: large enterprise promotion causes short-term +60% demand for 6 weeks, causing burst-capacity exposure and potential GPU spot premium
Scenario E - Combined adverse: sustained -15% price + -10% demand (mix shift to low-revenue embeddings) leading to acute margin stress
lattice: Two-dimensional lattice with Price-change axis (-25% .. +10%) and Demand-change axis (-40% .. +80%). Each node stores: probability weight, projected monthly gross margin delta, suggested operational action (none, hiring-freeze, contract surge, slab-reprice, emergency credits). Probabilities seeded from historical price movement distribution and sales pipeline sensitivity. The lattice is aggregated to 3 risk bands: Green (expected), Yellow (elevated), Red (action required).
key_tables: Table 1: Monthly P&L projection by scenario (Revenue, Inference cost, Gross margin, Opex run-rate) - Jun–Dec 2026
Table 2: HC plan by role and quarter (FTEs, contractors, open req lead times) with cost per FTE and savings estimate if hiring paused
Table 3: Capacity commit exposure (Dedicated contractual minimums, expected unused capacity, penalty schedule)
Table 4: Sensitivity summary: impact on margin and runway for +/-1%, +/-5%, +/-10% price shocks and demand shifts
Table 5: Rapid actions cost-benefit (quantization rollout, autoscaler tuning, short-term spot vs reserved mix) with implementation time and expected delta to per-token cost
headcount_plan: Baseline plan (published May 2026): +22 net FTEs across Eng (serving runtime + infra) and SRE from Jul–Dec 2026 to support product launches
Triage plan (Yellow band): pause non-critical associate hiring (8 FTEs deferred), convert 4 planned hires to contractors for 3–6 months
Conservative plan (Red band): immediate hiring freeze across non-customer-facing roles, redeploy 6 engineers from new features to ops, open voluntary time-off & temporary furlough playbook
Critical roles protected: 2 SRE site leads, 3 infra GPU ops, security engineer (no freeze for these)
Contractor-to-hire conversion budget: assume 1.6x cost but shorter lead time; model includes switching 6 planned hires to contractors in worst-case
sensitivity_results: Central (no action): 12% price drop -> margin falls 9 ppt; runway reduces from 16 to ~13 months unless mitigated
With mitigation package (quantization + hiring pause): same 12% price drop -> margin loss limited to 4–5 ppt; runway preserved at ~15 months
Worst combined node (-15% price, -10% demand): gross margin halves from baseline 46% -> 23%; cash runway drops by ~6 months without contract renegotiation

Demand surge (+60% for 6 weeks) without burst-control: short-term token revenue +40% but GPU spot premium increases inference cost by +28%, net incremental margin small; recommend temporary higher-price slab for burst customers
Dedicated commit mismatch: unused committed capacity in scenario C leads to an incremental monthly cash drag of $420k for two quarters
triggers_and_thresholds: Trigger 1 (Price): 7-day rolling average realized ARPU per 1k tokens drops >=8% vs baseline -> enter Yellow band and implement hiring pause for noncritical roles
Trigger 2 (Demand): 30-day rolling active token volume drops >=12% vs forecast -> CFO review and hold on ramping reserved capacity
Trigger 3 (Margin): Gross margin drops >6 ppt month-over-month -> escalate to execs and implement mitigation bundle (quantization, variable pricing, SRE redeploy)
Trigger 4 (Dedicated utilization): Committed capacity utilization <65% for two consecutive months -> open contract negotiation and rebalancing options
Trigger 5 (Burst exposure): Spot GPU utilization >120% of reserved baseline for 7 consecutive days -> temporary slab-rate increase for new burst customers and open capacity procurement
recommended_mitigation: Short-term: fast-track quantization profile rollout for high-volume models (estimated per-token cost delta -25% when fully applied to 45% of workload)
Operational: ~6-week hiring pause on non-essential roles + contractor surge for critical infra tasks
Pricing: deploy temporary ‘burst premium’ slab for high short-term usage and negotiate minimums for new enterprise deals
Product: enable transparent per-route cost analytics in Console for top 10 accounts to reduce surprise and negotiate credits
Commercial: offer short-term limited credits only tied to SLA guarantees to reduce churn while protecting revenue
